prompt:
Research Canonical's official statement on how long an Ubuntu LTS release receives standard support, and how long with Ubuntu Pro / ESM. Cite Canonical's own page and quote the periods.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Canonical’s own position is that standard Ubuntu LTS security maintenance lasts 5 years for Main, while Ubuntu Pro/ESM extends coverage to 10 years, with an optional Legacy add-on to 15 years.

SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "LTS are released every two years and receive 5 years of standard security maintenance." | CLAIM: Canonical states the standard support/security-maintenance period for an Ubuntu LTS is 5 years.
SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "Ubuntu Pro is Canonical's enhanced security and support subscription for Ubuntu systems." | CLAIM: Canonical frames Ubuntu Pro as the subscription that adds security/support beyond standard LTS maintenance.
SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "It includes up to 15 years of security coverage (ESM and Legacy add-on), Kernel Livepatch, Landscape, FIPS 140-3 certified packages, and CIS hardening, and optional enterprise-grade support." | CLAIM: Canonical says Ubuntu Pro can provide up to 15 years of total security coverage when ESM and the Legacy add-on are included.
SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "ESM extends the life of LTS releases by providing 10 years of security updates for the 'Main' repository and also adds 10 years of security coverage for the 'Universe' repository." | CLAIM: Canonical’s stated Ubuntu Pro/ESM period is 10 years for Main, and also 10 years for Universe.
SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/about/release-cycle?product= | QUOTE: "At the end of the 10 year ESM period, the Legacy add-on can be purchased to cover additional 5 years of the lifetime of Ubuntu LTS, giving a total of 15 years security maintenance and support for LTS releases." | CLAIM: Canonical says the optional Legacy add-on extends the 10-year ESM period by another 5 years, for 15 years total.
SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/security/esm | QUOTE: "Ubuntu LTS gained popularity due to a 5-year security maintenance commitment for the operating system (specifically all packages in the 'main repository')." | CLAIM: Canonical again identifies the standard LTS commitment as 5 years, specifically for Main.
SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/security/esm | QUOTE: "The 'esm-apps' stream covers all 'Universe' packages for ten years from the release of the LTS." | CLAIM: Canonical states that ESM-apps covers Universe packages for 10 years from release.
SOURCE: https://ubuntu.com/security/esm | QUOTE: "The 'esm-infra' stream covers 'Main' packages for the period after the standard five year security maintenance of 'Main' packages ends." | CLAIM: Canonical states that ESM-infra covers Main after the initial 5-year period, supporting the 5 + 5 = 10-year ESM interpretation.
SOURCE: https://canonical.com/legal/ubuntu-pro-description | QUOTE: "End of Standard Support: a date (5 years after the Release Date) on which free standard security maintenance service for the Ubuntu Main repository of an Ubuntu LTS expires" | CLAIM: Canonical’s legal definition of standard support confirms that free standard security maintenance for Main lasts 5 years after release.
